name: Frostmother's Cradle
formed_by_story: Meltwater under the Oskeld glacier, cutting a cave through ice that closes behind it a little every winter and opens a little every summer, so the cave is a different cave each year.
who_was_here: Whatever the ice caught. It is all still here, and you can see most of it.
story: The Cradle holds shapes. A wolf mid-stride, four feet off the floor, in clear ice. A clan banner. A hand. The clans will not come here because the ice keeps what it takes, and keeping is the Frostmother's business, and she is not a story.
unique_object: ice that holds the shapes of what froze in it, lit from behind

beats.note: A blue mouth in the glacier's foot, running with meltwater on any day above freezing.
A meltwater run, scalloped, glass-smooth underfoot, sloping down faster than it looks.
The gallery. Daylight comes through eight feet of ice above and turns the whole room blue. The shapes start here.
Where last winter closed the cave. It is open by a shoulder's width.
A meltwater pool, still, so clear that it reads as air until you step in it.
The Cradle: a dome of clear ice with a century of caught things suspended in the walls, arranged the way a room is arranged.
A crevasse climbing back to the surface, wide enough to chimney up if your hands hold.

shortcut.note: Chimney up once, and the rope you fix stays fixed.

encounters.note: Scree-hags; they come out of the pool, which reads as air.
What the ice kept and let go of: bone and rock that walked in here and was held, and walks again.
